title: Benefit Administration Manual, Chapter 2: How a Meal Status Determination Reaches the Students of a Household (School Nutrition Services Meal Account)
content:
This chapter governs which students' School Nutrition Services Meal Accounts take a status from a determination, and which status a student holds when more than one source applies.

**2.1** A determination reaches students according to the status's reach as set in the schedule of meal statuses (all students in the household, the individual student, or not applicable).

**2.2** An approved household application (reach: all students in the household) gives its status to every student of the household who has a meal account, from the determination date.

**2.3** A direct certification match of any one student in the household with a program on the direct certification list (SNAP, TANF, FDPIR, Medicaid) extends Free Meal Status (Direct Certification) to every student of the household.

**2.4** A categorical designation recorded on a student record (homeless under McKinney-Vento, foster care, migrant, runaway) reaches only that student, and a prior-year carryover reaches only the student who held the prior-year status.

**2.5** When several sources apply to the same student, the student holds the status with the lowest status precedence number, and a source of lower precedence never replaces it; when the higher source ends, the student takes the best status that still applies.

**2.6** Statuses of different students in the same household are decided separately, so siblings may hold different statuses.

## Worked cases (hypothetical household)

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| One child matches SNAP; the household has three children with meal accounts | all three hold Free Meal Status (Direct Certification) |
| One child is designated as in foster care; a sibling has no other source | the designated child holds Free Meal Status (Categorical Eligibility); the sibling's status is decided separately |
| A child holds Free Meal Status (Direct Certification), rank 2, and the household's application is approved for reduced price, rank 5 | the child keeps rank 2; the reduced-price source never replaces it |
| The categorical designation (rank 1) of a child ends while an approved free application (rank 3) still applies | the child takes Free Meal Status (Household Application), the best status that still applies |
| Only the older sibling held reduced-price status last year | only that sibling holds the carryover status |
